clinician.final_diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma of Müllerian Gland Type (AMGT) of the Vulva
clinician.trajectory_summary: A female patient in her 60s presented with a vulvar mass on the left labium minus. Excisional biopsy revealed a 32 mm nodule with cribriform and papillary architecture, moderate cytological atypia, and mitotic index of 31 per 10 HPF. Immunohistochemistry demonstrated strong positivity for estrogen receptors (90-100%), CK7, CAM5.2, and GATA3, with negativity for progesterone receptors, GCDDP-15, SOX10, p63, and CK20. HER-2 was equivocal (2+) but FISH-negative. No lymphovascular or perineural invasion was observed in the initial biopsy. Staging workup including clinical examination, breast imaging, chest CT, gastrointestinal tract study, and whole-body PET-FDG showed no evidence of primary breast or other malignancy, with hypermetabolic activity isolated to the left vulvar lesion. A second pathological review described ductal architecture organized in nests and cords with infiltrative growth pattern, moderate-to-high nuclear atypia, mitotic index of 20 per 10 HPF, with lymphovascular and perineural invasion present and margins intercepted by tumor. The morphological features (cribriform and papillary architecture, ductal organization) combined with the distinctive immunohistochemical profile (ER+, CK7+, CAM5.2+, GATA3+, PR-, SOX10-, p63-, CK20-) are characteristic of adenocarcinoma of Müllerian gland type.

Immunohistochemistry demonstrated strong positivity for estrogen receptors (90-100%), CK7, CAM5.2, and GATA3, with negativity for progesterone receptors, GCDDP-15, SOX10, p63, and CK20. Staging workup including clinical examination, breast imaging, chest CT, gastrointestinal tract study, and whole-body PET-FDG showed no evidence of primary breast or other malignancy, with hypermetabolic activity isolated to the left vulvar lesion. A second pathological review described ductal architecture organized in nests and cords with infiltrative growth pattern, moderate-to-high nuclear atypia, mitotic index of 20 per 10 HPF, with lymphovascular and perineural invasion present and margins intercepted by tumor. The morphological features (cribriform and papillary architecture, ductal organization) combined with the distinctive immunohistochemical profile (ER+, CK7+, CAM5.2+, GATA3+, PR-, SOX10-, p63-, CK20-) are characteristic of adenocarcinoma of Müllerian gland type.
